# Transcript renderer overview

The renderer turns each chat message into styled terminal rows. A message is a list of blocks, and every block kind owns its own presentation: Markdown text is parsed once and cached by content hash, tool calls render a one-line title plus a capped body, and diffs are computed line by line with three lines of context around each hunk. Wrapping happens last, at the width the terminal has right now, so a resize re-wraps cached lines instead of re-parsing them. The only block that is re-rendered on every frame while a reply streams is the tail block, which is why a long unbroken paragraph, an open code fence, or a half-received table is the worst case for the streaming path and the best case for a benchmark.

## Pipeline

1. **Serialize** each block into logical lines.
   - Markdown headings, emphasis, `inline code`, and [links](https://example.com/docs/render) keep their styles.
   - Tool calls render a title row plus a capped body.
     - Execute output keeps its ANSI colour and drops everything above the cap.
     - Diffs show only the changed hunks.
       - Added lines are green, removed lines are red, context is dim.
2. **Wrap** the logical lines to the terminal width.
3. **Commit** finished blocks to scrollback and keep the live tail mutable.

## Cost model

| Stage | Runs | Cached by | Typical cost |
| --- | :---: | --- | ---: |
| Parse Markdown | once per block | content hash | 40 us |
| Highlight code | once per fence | language + text | 120 us |
| Diff | once per edit | old + new text | 300 us |
| Wrap | every width change | width | 15 us |
| Paint | every frame | nothing | 5 us |

> The tail block is re-rendered on every chunk. Keep it small.
>
> A second paragraph inside the quote, with `code` and a [link](https://example.com/quote).

See <https://example.com/architecture> for the full picture, or the ~~old~~ current notes in `docs/src/architecture.md`.
A few snippets show the shapes the renderer has to handle.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for crate in core render widgets; do
  cargo test -p "$crate" --quiet || { echo "failed: $crate" >&2; exit 1; }
done
```
